texts.facts: 3. The brief facts of the case are that the complainant Shri S.B. Agrawal on 14.10.2005 visited the shop of the respondent - accused along with witness running in the name of Shri Hari Gruh Udhyog, where the respondent - accused was present. That, the complainant had purchased 3 packets of Palak Mathiya upon payment of Rs.135/- from the accused and the prescribed notice was also issued. That, in the presence of panch witness, three samples of the 'Palak Mathiya' were procured and sealed after following due procedure. That, one sample was forwarded on the next day with a memorandum, Form No. VII to the Public Analyst, Bhuj and two parts of samples were sent to Local Health Authority for analysis. That, the report of the Public Analyst shows that the sample of 'Palak Mathiya' is adulterated under Section 2(ia)(a) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, as the sample does not comply with the standards laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, in respect of the fat content. That, after obtaining the sanction of the local health authority as required under Section 20 of the Act, the Food Inspector filed complaint in the Court of learned Magistrate, Nadiad for the alleged offences under the provisions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. That, the learned Magistrate acquitted the accused and therefore, the State has preferred this appeal. 4. Learned APP Ms. Jirga Zaveri for the State has submitted that all the formalities including sanction and others is being carried out by the prosecution, however, the learned Magistrate has acquitted the accused and thereby committed an error and therefore, this appeal may be allowed.
